metadata.note_on_EOU: EOU answer markings in source represent unconfirmed guesses. Correct answers here are determined independently from platform knowledge and source content.

questions.question: Which phases are included in a typical OneStream implementation project?

options.A: Analyze, Design, Build, Test, and Rollout

questions.explanation: A is correct: a typical OneStream project follows five phases — Analyze, Design, Build, Test, and Rollout. B is incorrect — this omits the Analyze and Design phases. C is incorrect — this skips the Build and Test phases. D is incorrect — Discover and Deploy are not the standard OneStream project phase names.

questions.question: What happens during the Rollout Phase of a OneStream project?

options.A: End users fully test a prototype and provide feedback on updated reports
options.B: The client evaluates the results of the Testing Phase to determine whether the system is ready to go live
options.C: Testing is conducted to confirm that users across all time zones can access the system
options.D: The build team finalizes all dimension hierarchies and application configuration

questions.explanation: B is correct: during the Rollout Phase, the organization evaluates the outcome of the Testing Phase to determine whether the client is ready to go live with the system. A is incorrect — end user prototype testing is a Test Phase activity. C is incorrect — confirming system access across time zones happens during testing, before Rollout. D is incorrect — finalizing dimension hierarchies happens during the Build Phase.

questions.question: Which task is a key component of the Test Phase in a OneStream implementation?
questions.explanation: B is correct: User Acceptance Training (UAT) is a key component of the Test Phase — it ensures that end users are trained and can validate the system against business requirements before go-live. A is incorrect — Prototyping occurs during Design/Build. C is incorrect — finalizing dimension structure is a Build Phase activity. D is incorrect — configuring Application Properties is a Build Phase activity.

questions.question: Which categories are available for all Dimension Types in the Member Properties in OneStream?

options.B: General, FX Rates, Security, and Settings

questions.explanation: D is correct: the four universal categories in Member Properties for all Dimension Types are General, Descriptions, Security, and Settings. A is incorrect — Workflow is not a universal member property category. B is incorrect — FX Rates is specific to certain dimension types, not universal. C is incorrect — Aggregation is not one of the four universal categories; Security replaces it.

questions.question: Which XML Load files can be created with the Excel Metadata Builder in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the Excel Metadata Builder can create XML load files for both Dimensions and Workflow Profiles — separate templates exist for each. A is incorrect — a Workflow template also exists, making Dimensions-only incomplete. B is incorrect — the Dimension template is also a core use case. D is incorrect — Cube Views are not loaded via XML through the Excel Metadata Builder.

questions.question: Which dimensions are assigned in the Default Scenario Type in OneStream?
questions.explanation: D is correct: the Entity and Scenario dimensions are assigned in the Default Scenario Type — other Scenario Types refer back to Default for these two dimensions, which is why they appear grayed out in other Scenario Types. A is incorrect — Account and Flow are Account-Type dimensions, not what is assigned in Default. B is incorrect — Flow is an Account-Type dimension, not assigned in Default. C is incorrect — while Scenario is correct, Account incorrectly replaces Entity.

questions.question: Which two dimensions should be designated for only the Default Scenario Type?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Entity and Scenario are the two dimensions designated for only the Default Scenario Type — other Scenario Types reference Default for these dimensions rather than defining their own. A is incorrect — Account and UD1 are Account-Type dimensions that vary per Scenario Type for extensibility; they are not exclusive to Default. C is incorrect — Account is an Account-Type dimension used across Scenario Types. D is incorrect — Account is used across Scenario Types for extensibility, not exclusive to Default.

questions.question: What are FX Rate Types able to be set up for in OneStream?
questions.explanation: B is correct: FX Rate Types can be set up by Cube and by Scenario — allowing different exchange rate configurations for different cubes and scenarios. A is incorrect — FX Rate Types are not configured at the Entity or Account level. C is incorrect — Period and Year are Time dimension members, not the configuration levels for FX Rate Types. D is incorrect — Assets/Liabilities and Revenue/Expenses describe account categories that rates are applied to, not what FX Rate Types are set up for.

questions.question: Which Dimension Type does Horizontal Extensibility refer to for the utilization of Extensibility in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Horizontal Extensibility refers to the Scenario dimension type — it allows different Scenario Types to have different levels of Account-type dimension detail within the same cube. A is incorrect — Entity is the dimension associated with Vertical Extensibility, not Horizontal. B is incorrect — Account is an Account-Type dimension affected by Horizontal Extensibility but is not the driving dimension type. D is incorrect — Flow is an Account-Type dimension and is not the Horizontal Extensibility dimension type.

questions.question: What is Horizontal Extensibility assigned to in an application after the Extensibility has been created?
questions.explanation: C is correct: after Horizontal Extensibility is created, it is assigned to Scenario Types — this allows each Scenario Type to have its own set of Account-type dimension members for different levels of detail. A is incorrect — Account Dimensions are what Horizontal Extensibility modifies, not what it is assigned to. B is incorrect — Horizontal Extensibility is assigned at the Scenario Type level, not Cube Type. D is incorrect — Entity Members are associated with Vertical Extensibility, not Horizontal.

questions.question: Which Scenario Type should have its Account-type Dimensions set to RootXXXDim in a OneStream Cube on the Cube Dimensions tab?
questions.explanation: D is correct: the Account-type Dimensions should be set to RootXXXDim for the Default Scenario Type — this establishes the root-level dimension assignment from which all other Scenario Types extend or reference. A is incorrect — Budget references Account-type dimensions from Default or extends them through Horizontal Extensibility. B is incorrect — Actual follows the same pattern as Budget. C is incorrect — Forecast likewise inherits from Default. Default is the base configuration.

questions.question: What controls the overall read/write access to Entity data in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Entity Security controls the overall read/write access to Entity data — it provides the most flexibility for applying security groups and has the widest range of available security settings. A is incorrect — Extensibility determines dimension structure and sharing; it does not control data access rights. B is incorrect — Workflow controls the data collection process, not Entity data access rights. D is incorrect — Cube Properties configures how a cube operates, not read/write security on entity data.

questions.question: The IC Dimension is required for intercompany account transactions. What Dimension is the IC Dimension based on?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the IC (Intercompany) Dimension is based on the Entity Dimension — it references entity members to identify intercompany trading partners for tracking and eliminating intercompany balances. A is incorrect — Account members identify transaction types, not trading partners. B is incorrect — Scenario identifies the type of data being stored, not trading partners. D is incorrect — Flow identifies data movement types and is not the basis for the IC Dimension.

questions.question: What is the process of presenting data that lives in the Cube with data that lives outside of the Cube called?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Analytic Blend is the process of presenting cube data alongside data that lives outside of the cube — it enables combining cube data with external relational data for unified reporting and analysis. A is incorrect — Rotational Blend is not a valid OneStream term. C is incorrect — Stub Blend is not a valid OneStream term. D is incorrect — Dynamic Cube Services (DCS) is a related technology, but the broader process of combining cube and non-cube data is called Analytic Blend.

questions.question: What color font indicates that a member is inherited when shown in a hierarchy in OneStream?
questions.explanation: C is correct: inherited members are displayed in gray font in the OneStream hierarchy — this visual indicator distinguishes inherited members from native members in the current context. A is incorrect — black font indicates native (non-inherited) members. B is incorrect — blue typically indicates drillable values in cube views, not inherited hierarchy members. D is incorrect — orange is not the standard indicator for inherited members.

questions.question: Which tasks are associated with the Level 2 Data Unit in OneStream?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the tasks of a Level 2 Data Unit are Load, Clear, and Lock. A is incorrect — Confirm is a workflow step, but Lock is the Level 2 Data Unit task, not Confirm. C is incorrect — Import is the mechanism for bringing data in, but Load is the correct Level 2 task term. D is incorrect — Import is not the Level 2 task designation; Load is correct.

questions.subtopic: Importing Data — Origin Dimension and Base Input Profiles
questions.question: What function can a user perform because of the relationship between the Origin Dimension and the Base Input Profiles?

options.B: Configure the Data Source and Transformation Rules for all Child Import Workflow Profiles
options.C: Control and lock individual methods of entering data
options.D: View the audit trail for all data submissions

questions.explanation: C is correct: the relationship between the Origin Dimension and the Base Input Profiles allows users to control and lock individual methods of entering data — each child input type (Import, Forms, Adj) maps to an Origin member, enabling granular locking per entry method. A is incorrect — troubleshooting Import errors is not the specific function of this relationship. B is incorrect — configuring Data Sources and Transformation Rules is done at the Import child profile level, not enabled by the Origin relationship specifically. D is incorrect — audit trails are accessed through Drill Down and Cell Status.

questions.subtopic: Importing Data — Is Optional Data Load
questions.question: When data needs to be loaded to some periods but not all during a Historical Data load, which property provides a quick way to complete the Workflow if no data is loaded to a period?

options.B: Flow Type No Data Zero View Override
options.D: Force Balance Accounts to YTD View

questions.explanation: C is correct: Is Optional Data Load set to True provides a quick way to complete the Workflow when no data is loaded to a period — the profile gains a 'Complete Workflow' icon the user can click to advance without loading data. A is incorrect — Can Load Unrelated Entities enables Central Input profiles to load across unrelated entities; it does not handle periods with no data. B is incorrect — Flow Type No Data Zero View Override controls display of zero/NoData values, not workflow completion logic. D is incorrect — Force Balance Accounts to YTD View is a display/calculation setting for balance accounts.

questions.question: Which property on a Form Template controls if a form is available quarterly, monthly, yearly, or half-yearly?
questions.explanation: C is correct: the Frequency property on a Form Template controls how often the form appears — options include monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, and yearly. A is incorrect — Time is a OneStream dimension, not a Form Template frequency property. B is incorrect — Required (Form Requirement Level) controls whether the form must be completed before proceeding, not how often it appears. D is incorrect — Form Type determines whether the form uses a Cube View, Dashboard, or Spreadsheet; it does not control frequency.

questions.question: Which Parameter Type does not prompt the user in OneStream?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the Literal Value parameter type does not prompt the user — it holds a hard-coded or centralized value applied automatically without requiring user input. A is incorrect — Input Value parameters prompt the user to enter or change a value. C is incorrect — Delimited List parameters prompt the user with a dropdown of predefined options. D is incorrect — Member List parameters prompt the user with a dropdown of dimension members.

questions.question: Which View Dimension Members are used for entering commentary in OneStream? (Select 2.)
questions.explanation: C and D are correct: Annotation and Footnote are two View Dimension Members that can receive commentary — along with Assumptions, AuditComment, and VarianceExplanation, they provide structured commentary locations. A is incorrect — YTD is a numeric aggregation View member; it does not accept commentary. B is incorrect — RestofYear is a numeric View member for remaining periods; it is not a commentary member.

questions.question: Which type of calculation is an in-memory calculation that runs on demand when a cell containing a dynamic member formula is requested?
questions.explanation: B is correct: a Dynamic calculation is an in-memory calculation that runs on demand when a cell containing a dynamic member formula is requested — it computes a value for a single cell without storing the result. A is incorrect — a Stored calculation is persisted in the cube and runs as part of DUCS, not on demand. C is incorrect — Force Consolidation is a calc run type, not the name of the on-demand in-memory calculation category. D is incorrect — Data Management calculations are orchestrated through DM steps and sequences, distinct from Dynamic calculations.

questions.question: Which type of calculation is a persisted calculation that runs as part of the Data Unit Calculation Sequence (DUCS)?
questions.explanation: B is correct: a Stored calculation is a persisted calculation that runs as part of the Data Unit Calculation Sequence (DUCS) — its result is written to and stored in the cube. A is incorrect — a Dynamic calculation runs on demand in memory and is not persisted. C is incorrect — Force Calculate is a Calc Type option that forces recalculation; it is not the name of a persisted calculation category. D is incorrect — Consolidate is the entity hierarchy roll-up process, not the category name for persisted member formula calculations.

questions.question: What does the CN Status Code represent in OneStream?

options.A: The data for this intersection has not changed since the last calculation
options.B: Consolidate because data for a child Entity has changed
options.C: Calculate data since an import was run or data was entered
options.D: Translate the data to the reporting currency

questions.explanation: B is correct: the CN Status Code represents that Consolidation is needed because data for a child Entity has changed — the parent entity needs to be reconsolidated to reflect updated child data. A is incorrect — data unchanged since last calculation shows an OK status, not CN. C is incorrect — needing to calculate after an import or data entry shows a CA status, not CN. D is incorrect — needing to translate data shows a TR status, not CN.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Confirmation Rules in OneStream?

options.A: To protect the data from being changed after validation
options.C: To act as visual checklists of Cube data validations embedded in the Workflow
options.D: To certify that the workflow has been completed by authorized users

questions.explanation: C is correct: Confirmation Rules are visual checklists of Cube data validations embedded in the Workflow — they run whenever a Workflow includes a Confirm step, providing pass/fail/warning indicators to verify data quality. A is incorrect — protecting data from changes is handled by workflow locking. B is incorrect — triggering calculations is the role of Process step Calculation Definitions. D is incorrect — certifying workflow completion is the function of Certification Questions and the Certify step.
